summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, and prior left index finger amputation due to steal syndrome was admitted for a dehisced wound with signs of infection, including swelling, pain, and prior pus. Cultures from clinic identified E. coli, and the patient had been started on Augmentin. He was admitted for IV antibiotics, pain control, and wound care. Imaging showed no osteomyelitis. Treatment included IV Zosyn, transition to oral Bactrim and ciprofloxacin, daily Betadine soaks, and hand elevation. His diabetes was poorly controlled with glucose levels in the 200–300 mg/dL range, prompting consultation with Endocrinology and initiation of glargine insulin with a sliding scale. The patient remained afebrile, stable, and pain-controlled throughout the stay. He was discharged home on a 7-day course of oral antibiotics, continued insulin regimen, and instructions for wound care and follow-up with Hand Clinic and Endocrinology.
